story.value: The name iridium comes from the Latin Iris, the Greek goddess of rainbows, because the element's salt solutions come in a variety of colours.
The British chemist Smithson Tennant discovered iridium and osmium at the same time, in 1803.
The French chemist H. V. Collet-Descotils also discovered iridium independently.

uses.value: Iridium is mainly used as a hardening agent for platinum.
Iridium is used for electrical contacts.
The standard meter bar was made from an alloy of platinum and iridium.
